scenes.title: One agent on a laptop is not a team setup

cues.text: A coding agent on a laptop works well for one person.
A team asks harder questions.
Each person runs agents in a different way, and nobody sees all of them.
Who runs the agents, on which machine, and with which keys?
How do you follow them, steer them and review their work?
How do you merge safely, and keep credentials away from agent code?

scenes.title: Tickets in, merged pull requests out

cues.text: Symphony turns tickets into work orders, from Linear or a GitHub Projects board.
A webhook starts the agent. When the work is done, it opens a ready pull request.
Each attempt runs in its own pod. The tracker, App and chat keys stay outside.
You follow, steer or take over any agent from Tern, the CLI or MCP.
cues.say: You follow, steer or take over any agent from Tern, the C L I or M C P.

cues.text: Two models review each pull request. A train merges only the head that CI tested.
cues.say: Two models review each pull request. A train merges only the head that C I tested.

cues.text: Admins choose a model for each role, and store the API keys in one place.
After each ticket, a learnings pull request can teach the repository. A person merges it.
Notices go to Slack or Discord.
An assistant in chat answers questions and plans tickets.
A first-run setup checks each value against the real service before it saves it.

scenes.title: Tested end to end, open and self-hosted

cues.text: The vendor mocks follow each vendor's published specification.
Real agents passed all 8 scenarios with Linear and Slack, and 4 with GitHub and Discord.
cues.say: Real agents passed all eight scenarios with Linear and Slack, and four with GitHub and Discord.

cues.text: The merger was certified on a real GitHub repository, with real CI.
cues.say: The merger was certified on a real GitHub repository, with real C I.

cues.text: Each defect that these runs found now has a regression test.
On kind, a full Kubernetes run took 275 seconds.
cues.say: On kind, a full Kubernetes run took two hundred seventy-five seconds.

cues.text: Symphony is open source under the MIT License. You host it yourself.
cues.say: Symphony is open source under the M I T License. You host it yourself.

cues.text: Models use API keys or cloud credentials. There is no OAuth or subscription login.
cues.say: Models use API keys or cloud credentials. There is no O Auth or subscription login.

scenes.title: Where it fits, and where it does not

cues.text: It fits a team that plans work in tickets and reviews code in pull requests.
A repository can send disputed findings to a maintainer instead of the arbiter.
Your code must be on GitHub, and the tracker must be Linear or GitHub Projects.
You need Kubernetes. One VM with k3s is enough.
cues.say: You need Kubernetes. One V M with K 3 S is enough.

cues.text: Local mode runs on one machine, with no container. Use it to try Symphony.
Linear, Slack and Discord were certified against mocks, not the real services.
Install the API and Redis with one kubectl command.
cues.say: Install the API and Red-iss with one kube control command.

cues.text: Then run symphony setup, or open Setup in Tern.
Each step is checked before it is saved.
The video list in the docs covers each part in depth.
